patches.reason: In this older toys module, backgroundRemoveAllToys filters the toy map with a key/value closure but then uses the whole Map.Entry (it) as the state name, so the release event name became "…-key={…}" and set() got an entry instead of the state key. The selected state is the key (the filter tests stateIs(s)); the newer toys.groovy also addresses it.key. Use it.key.

The main menu filtered its option and request records by calling the closure stored in each record (it.cond()), which the converter cannot lower inside findAll, so the menu came out empty. Filter in plain loops that call each condition through a local variable, in the same order; the request menu builds its label list in its own statement and adds '...nevermind' to a new list instead of the caller's list, which the caller rebuilds before each menu anyway.

getProp read a storage key through a Java method reference (this.&loadBoolean and the like, called with f.apply), which the converter cannot lower, so every toy.* property read its default. Read the key with load(), which returns the stored value whatever its type, and keep loadB, loadI, and loadS as names so that no call site changes; each toy.* key is only ever saved with one type, so the typed filter of the legacy loaders made no difference.

The scheduled events were Event and NamedEvent class instances, loaded with loadMap and collectEntries and found with a map each() loop, none of which converts, so no event was ever found and the main loop restarted the script forever. Keep each event as the plain map [time, func, arg] that was already saved, load it with load(), add it with put(), and find the next one in a loop over the keys, in the same order and with the same tie rule; the null checks of the result are written out as e != null.

localTimeOffset read the zone offset from java.time zone rules and getDayNum used Math.floorDiv, neither of which converts, so both returned null and every day and clock-time calculation failed. Take the offset from the local clock instead (local hour and minute minus the UTC time of day, rounded to the 15-minute steps that zone offsets use and folded into -12..+14 hours) and use intdiv, which equals floorDiv for the positive times involved.

getRandomSession drew from a java.util.Random seeded with the session start, which has no TeaseScript equivalent, so it returned null and every list index built from it failed. Derive the number from the same seed with one Park-Miller step instead: it stays constant for the play session as before, but the numbers differ from Java's; a missing seed, where Java failed, gives 0.

compose() built its sentence with a collect/join/capitalize chain and gagText() with String.toList() and a list sum(), which do not convert, so every composed line came out null. Pick one text per group in a loop and join the parts, write the consonant lists out, and join the gagged characters with join(""), with the same results (an empty text gives "" where the legacy sum() gave "null").

executeTrigger called each handler's closure as a record property inside forEach (th.func(...)), which does not convert, so no trigger handler ran (availability statistics and summon counters). Call each matching handler through a local variable in a loop, in the same order and with the same argument.

The script detected the operating system to speak texts with the Windows or macOS speech program (sayCommand(...).execute()); owner decision: speech output is ignored. Leave osName unset, so that canTalk() is false and the voice settings are not offered, make say() do nothing, and let sayCommand() return an empty command instead of null for an unknown system, which only the unreachable voice test reads.

getDomme evaluated the Groovy data files images/toy/domme.groovy, images/toy/<domme>/person.groovy, and set.groovy at runtime (new File, Eval.me), which a package cannot do, so DOMME stayed null and every image lookup by DOMME.id failed. Write the title and the two person files out as a dict, with the id as before. The session plans in domme.groovy are left out: only sessionPlay reads them, and it evaluates their expression strings with Eval, which does not convert either.

getBooleanG reused its boolean shuffle parameter for the number getRandom(2), which TeaseScript rejects because a variable keeps one type. Store getRandom(2) != 0, which is true exactly when the number was truthy.

hasSessionToy returned false for a toy not yet fetched in the session and its count otherwise, but useSessionToy compared that with < and getRestraints subtracted it, which failed in Groovy for false. Return 0 for a missing toy (callers that test its truth see the same) and let getRestraints test for a missing toy with containsKey, which is what its == false meant.

The image spec [nDRESSED, [TITS,PUSSY,ASS]] mixed a text and a list in one list, which TeaseScript rejects. Wrap the text in a one-element list; multiplexTags turns every element into a list ([]+t) before it combines them, so the images chosen are the same.

playBondage kept its game choice in one variable that held false or the number 1 or 2, which TeaseScript rejects because a variable keeps one type. Use 0 for no game: the variable is only tested for truth, compared with 1, and switched on 1 and 2, where 0 behaves as false did, and the random draws happen in the same order.

postChastity stored the index of a forced choice in its boolean answer variable sh, which TeaseScript rejects because a variable keeps one type; nothing reads sh after that choice, so ask without storing the result.

getRecentAvail summed a collected list with sum(), which Groovy defines as null for an empty list, so its result may be null and the comparisons of setupInitial do not compile. Every caller asks for at least one day, so add the days in a loop from 0, in the same order, with the same result.

getSoft keeps a wait time only when timing is set and guarded each change with timing, which a type checker cannot connect with the nullable wait time. Guard the changes with waitTime != null, which is true exactly when timing was set.

anyToys, backgroundRemoveAllToys, and removeAllToys filtered the toy map with key/value closures (any, findAll, collect), which do not convert, so anyToys returned null and worn toys were never removed. Use loops over the keys instead: anyToys stops at the first worn toy as any() did, and the other two first collect the worn toys and then act on them, in the same order.

DOMME started as null until main() loads it, so every DOMME.id read was typed as possibly null. Start it as an empty map: main() loads the domme before anything reads it, so the value read never changes.

strokes counted its loop in it without a declaration, a script binding variable that the converter turns into a nullable global. No other code reads it, so count in a local variable instead; the case closure {it < 2} keeps its own parameter.

bedtime and bedtimeCheck assigned imgSpec without a declaration, a script binding variable that the converter turns into a nullable global. Each sets it before reading it and no other code reads it, so declare it locally.

beginPlan built its message as (hadtoys ? [...] : []) + naked ? [...] : [], where + binds before ?:, so the list plus a boolean was always true and the message was always only "put your clothes back on." even when the toys had to come off. Group each choice as intended, so the message names the toys, the clothes, or both.

suckDildo kept its sound loops in local closures; suck and suckBeat capture other local closures, which TeaseScript cannot express, so those sounds were skipped, and a closure called with mixed text and number arguments does not convert either. Make the three closures toy methods (suckPlayWait, suckRepeat, suckBeat) with the same bodies, defined before suckDildo, and call them directly.

writeLines capitalized the result of compose(), which may be null for an empty group list, so the call does not compile; compose() already capitalizes its result and the line groups are never empty, so use its result as it is.
perm(String i) passed it, which is not defined there, to can() instead of its parameter i; nothing calls perm, so pass i.
